speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will speak after me on matters regarding governance on data in general.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The incident has caused anxiety and distress to the affected persons.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This matter is especially delicate as it involves persons living with HIV.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Members have asked several questions regarding the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: So, let me first give a brief account on what happened, the actions we took, and why.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some have asked whether MOH had known about Brochez's possible access to HIV Registry information in 2012 when he first made a complaint to MOH.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Brochez was then a partner of Dr Ler Teck Siang who was the Head of the National Public Health Unit (NPHU), and they had lived together.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In November 2012, Brochez alleged that Ler had disclosed information about Brochez to others.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: He later also claimed that Ler had shared screenshots of his HIV status with others.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Despite multiple attempts by MOH to engage him, Brochez did not provide any evidence to support his allegation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: He was uncooperative and evasive, and rejected or postponed meetings with MOH on several occasions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At one point, he even informed MOH officers that he was leaving Singapore and did not want to continue with the investigation into his allegation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Due to his uncooperative attitude, the investigation could not make much headway.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Nevertheless, we re-assigned Ler to another role in May 2013, and kept up the investigation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ler's access to the live HIV Registry was terminated after his re-assignment.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In the course of our investigations, MOH discovered in December 2013 that Brochez may have submitted fake HIV blood tests to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) in order to retain his Employment Pass.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We informed MOM and also made a Police report.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH's investigations in 2012 and 2013 were on Brochez's allegation that Ler had revealed Brochez's HIV status to others.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At no point in 2012 or 2013 did MOH have basis to suspect that Brochez had access to, or was in possession of, the data in the HIV Registry.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Between 2014 and 2016, the Police and MOH investigated whether Brochez had submitted fake blood tests, and whether Ler had abetted this process and provided false information to investigators.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These investigations were difficult as Brochez continued to be uncooperative and initially refused to provide a statement to the Police.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Police eventually recorded a statement from Brochez in May 2014, after he was stopped trying to leave Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: When interviewed, Brochez lied to the Police that it was his blood that was tested during a HIV test conducted in November 2013.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH then ordered Brochez to undergo a fresh blood test for HIV to verify his claim, but Brochez refused to cooperate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Police raided Ler's and Brochez's premises simultaneously and seized and secured all relevant materials.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These included their computers and electronic storage devices containing files with confidential information from the HIV Registry, files related to hospital services and to other infectious diseases, as well as other information likely used by Ler for his work, such as emails, HIV studies and reports.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Police searched through Brochez's email account and found that Brochez had sent the same screenshot that he had sent to Government authorities, as well as a portable document format (PDF) file of a further 46 records from the HIV Registry, to his mother.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Police then contacted Brochez's mother, who agreed to let the Police access her email account and deleted those records.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At this point, the Police had seized everything they found in Ler's and Brochez's possession and had done their best to ensure that no further confidential information remained with Ler and Brochez, including in their known online accounts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It was always recognised that there was a risk that Brochez could have hidden away some more information.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ler and Brochez were both charged in Court in June 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ler was charged both under the Penal Code and the Official Secrets Act (OSA).

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ler's charge sheet, which was public information, stated that he had had access to the HIV Registry as part of his position as the Head of NPHU in MOH, and that he had failed to take reasonable care of the information in the HIV Registry by failing to retain possession of a thumb drive on which he had saved the HIV Registry.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Brochez was charged for offences under the Misuse of Drugs Act, Penal Code and Infectious Diseases Act (IDA).

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) decides on the charges.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This was because there had been no wide dissemination of the information at that stage, and he had primarily used the information to complain to Government agencies, and he was already facing numerous fraud and drug-related charges, which carried far heavier penalties.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: AGC also assessed that any jail term under the OSA was likely to be concurrent with jail terms that he would serve under other offences.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Brochez was, therefore, issued with a stern warning for the OSA offence.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In its judgment, the Court found that Brochez had "deliberate  flout  the law for personal benefit", and that there was "not a single word of regret." Mr Speaker, Sir, let me now address questions as to whether MOH should have informed the public earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In 2016, MOH had to decide whether to inform the affected persons and whether to make a public announcement about the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On the one hand, there is the need to be transparent.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On the other hand, we need to consider the impact of an announcement on the affected persons with HIV – would it serve their interest or would it harm them instead?

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I discussed this with my medical colleagues in MOH.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They emphasised the need to pay particular attention to the concerns and needs of HIV patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A person's HIV status is a deeply emotional and personal matter.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some patients will experience high anxiety and distress from a disclosure or announcement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some will feel compelled to reveal their HIV status to family members or friends.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Relationships can be disrupted; lives can be changed.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We had to exercise care and judgement in making our decision, and the well-being of the affected persons weighed heavily in our considerations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One key factor was that there was then still no evidence that the confidential information had been disseminated to the public.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Brochez had sent the information to Government authorities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Police search was extensive and all relevant material found had been seized or deleted.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While there could be no guarantee, MOH had good reason to believe that the information had been secured and the risk of future exposure significantly mitigated.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ultimately, it was a judgement call to be made based on the information we had, and the considerations for and against an announcement, and the assessed risk of future public exposure of the information.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Two years later, in April 2018, Brochez was deported from Singapore after serving his sentence and we had no basis to keep him here.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In May 2018, after his deportation, Brochez sent a screenshot containing 31 records from the HIV Registry to several Government authorities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They were a subset of the 75 which Brochez had earlier revealed to authorities in May 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We considered again whether to inform the affected individuals and the public.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The relevant factors were similar to those in 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This time, we could not retrieve the screenshot of the 31 records in Brochez's possession because he was already out of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We did not make a public announcement as there was still no specific evidence that Brochez had more information beyond these 31 records.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Furthermore, as on previous occasions, Brochez had only shared it with Government authorities and not to any wider audience.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A public announcement would create anxiety and distress not just among the 31 persons but also other HIV patients whose names were in the Registry.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In September 2018, Ler was convicted for abetting Brochez to commit cheating, and also of providing false information to the Police and MOH.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ler has appealed and this is scheduled to be heard in March 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ler's charge under the OSA is currently "stood down".

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: That means that the OSA charge has been put aside for the moment, but it remains before the Courts and will be dealt with after proceedings on his other charges have concluded.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: AGC decided to go to trial against Ler on the cheating and false information charges first, as they were more serious and carried stiffer penalties.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The trial for his drug charges will be held next, as these also involve stiffer penalties, including mandatory caning.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: So that there is no doubt, let me say again that the OSA charge against Ler is still "live".

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: AGC will decide on the OSA charge, after proceedings on his other charges have concluded.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The most recent incident in January 2019 stood on a different footing from the earlier incidents.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It showed that Brochez probably still possessed the entire HIV Registry, beyond just the 31 records.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: He had also put the information online and provided the link to a non-Government party.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This new situation meant that the likelihood of the identities of affected persons being made public by Brochez had increased significantly.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We sought to quickly contact each of the affected individuals to inform them of the circumstances and also offer them assistance prior to the announcement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We worked with the Police and other relevant parties to disable access to the information as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In making those decisions, MOH had a responsibility to balance the opposing considerations and exercise judgement on what would best serve the interest of the affected persons and the public.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH made a judgement call, balancing the various considerations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is arguable that MOH should have made a different call.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But I reject any allegation that MOH sought to cover up the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On all three occasions, MOH's primary concern was the well-being of the persons on the HIV Registry.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Today, we still face the same dilemma as we did back in 2016 and 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We now know that Brochez retained some of the data after the Police seized all the files they could find in 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Quite possibly, he still has more files in his possession.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Should MOH now make known all that Brochez may, or may not, still have in his possession?

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Do we contact every person whose data may, or may not, be at risk?

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And in the process inflict more harm on people even though it may ultimately turn out that Brochez, in fact, does not have the information?

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Again, we have to assess and make a judgement call.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is consistent with the decision taken in 2016 and again in 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is based on what we believe to be the interest of the potentially affected persons.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Brochez is currently under Police investigation for various offences.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: He is believed to be in the US.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Police are engaging their American counterparts and are seeking their assistance in the investigations against Brochez.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Police will spare no effort pursuing all avenues to bring Brochez to justice.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Following our public announcement, a few parties have come forward to inform us that Brochez had, in fact, attempted to make contact with them in 2018, and had given them links to confidential information he had uploaded online.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have quickly worked with the authorities to similarly disable access to the online content.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have also been working with relevant parties to scan the Internet for indications of further sharing of the information.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There have thus far been no signs of further disclosure, but we will continue to monitor.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Should we detect any disclosure or online publication of the information, MOH will work with the relevant authorities and parties to take down the content and disable access to the data.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Here, I would like to remind everyone that the Police will not hesitate to take stern action, including prosecution, against anyone who possesses, communicates or uses any of the confidential data that has been disclosed.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Police will also not tolerate any harassment or intimidation, of any form, towards any person, arising from this leak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH has prioritised informing and supporting the affected individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have completed attempts to contact all the affected individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But we are unable to reach all of them, as many had dated contact information, given that the Registry went back to 1985.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many of the foreigners were work pass applicants who never worked in Singapore, or who previously worked here but are no longer in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Individuals who worry that they may be affected or who have concerns, can contact our hotline at 6325 9220.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We seek their understanding that to maintain confidentiality of the information, we have to verify the identity of the caller.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Officers manning our hotline will then provide information on the incident and direct callers to available avenues for support.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Anthea Ong, Assoc Prof Walter Theseira and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked about the measures taken to protect the psychological welfare of the affected individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We know that the affected persons may have concerns and may be worried about unfair treatment arising from this incident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Prior to calling patients, our medical social workers have helped to first identify those likely to require more support, so that designated officers can exercise extra care and provide additional support when calling them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If callers request to speak to our counsellors, are in distress, or require more advice and support, counsellors are on standby to speak with them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some affected individuals may prefer to discuss their concerns with those they are more familiar with, such as the medical social workers, nurses and doctors who have been supporting their ongoing care and treatment.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have arranged with the relevant public hospitals to have medical social workers and doctors onsite to attend to them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Agencies, such as the Life Insurance Association (LIA), MOM and the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) have provided public assurances on common concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Understandably, despite these efforts, some will continue to be concerned.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some may decline to return to care because of the fear of future disclosure.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some felt we should have just informed the affected individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A few wished they had not been called at all.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The anxiety and concerns which some individuals felt have also been carried in various online, broadcast and print articles in recent weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our medical social workers were themselves distressed by the news they had to break and felt the anguish that the patients experienced when they were told.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They had to conduct the calls carefully and gently and be alert to signs of distress so that they could help the patients appropriately.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At times, our medical social workers became the target of anger and blamed themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH’s national HIV Registry contains information of persons diagnosed with HIV in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are not unique in having such a registry.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Countries, such as the US and Canada, also maintain HIV registries containing identifiable information.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We need the Registry to monitor the HIV infection situation, conduct contact tracing, and assess disease prevention and management measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The data needs to be identifiable for purposes, such as contact tracing, to protect those who are contacts of HIV patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The security safeguards for the HIV Registry in 2012/2013 were in accordance with the prevailing Government policies on classified information and information technology (IT) security.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Staff were briefed on the policies, systems and processes, and regularly reminded of the sensitivity of the information, which they should access on a need-to-know basis.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: All of them signed an undertaking to observe confidentiality obligations under the OSA.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Prior to 2012, the HIV Registry was placed in a secured network drive.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The file could only be accessed and downloaded from Government issued computers, and was password protected.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: NPHU staff would need to download the HIV Registry in order to carry out routine data entry, contact tracing and analysis.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Staff were allowed to use personal thumb drives at that time, subject to adherence to data protection guidelines and policies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng asked about the additional measures undertaken to ensure data security.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In 2012, prior to the complaint from Brochez, the Registry database was migrated to a network-based system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: NPHU staff no longer had to download a database file stored on a network drive to do their work.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Instead, staff would call up records they require from the network-based system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With the implementation of a network-based Registry, the audit trail was also enhanced.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In 2014, alerts of multiple failed login attempts were incorporated into the system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH continues to follow the security policies from the Singapore Government Instruction Manual (IM) for the Security of Classified Information.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In tandem with the Government guidelines, we implemented several controls to tighten our systems.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Specifically for NPHU, MOH’s Chief Data Officer also conducted a data security review in 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This workstation is configured and locked down to prevent unauthorised removal of data.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In 2017, NPHU also complied with Government-wide policy to disable the use of unauthorised portable storage devices on official computers and only allow the use of authorised and encrypted thumb drives.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To give greater attention to data usage and safeguards, we had also set up a Data Analytics Group in April 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Within the group, a Data Governance Division was set up to formulate policies, practices and guidelines for MOH and its agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The aim is to protect and secure access to health sector data, in accordance with data protection requirements in the Government IMs and the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), and other MOH sectoral legislation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In light of the recent incident, and the increased prevalence of data use across the healthcare sector, it is important to ensure that data security and governance policies are strictly adhered to on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH will expand the role and resourcing of this unit.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will include within it a specific mandate and team to look into the compliance and audits of data access and use.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Several Members have called for destigmatisation of HIV and asked how we can protect people living with HIV from discrimination.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Stigmatisation is an issue that all of us are concerned with.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: HIV, therefore, continues to be a serious infectious disease that MOH closely monitors and actively manages for public health reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But clinically, HIV treatment has vastly improved over the years, and early treatment can delay disease progression and improve the quality of life.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Over the years, MOH has increased financial support and lowered the financial barriers for HIV treatment through MediSave and MediFund.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Since 2014, HIV anti-retroviral drugs can be supported under the Medication Assistance Fund (MAF).

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Special outreach efforts have also been made for specific groups.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For instance, it is part of standard antenatal testing at our public hospitals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Support from doctors, medical social workers and healthcare workers is also widely available in public hospitals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Generally, every HIV patient in public healthcare institutions is assigned to a medical social worker to provide assistance upon their diagnosis.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH has, therefore, been working with stakeholders to raise awareness of the disease and reduce stigma for the disease.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: More recently, the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices call for employers to treat employees fairly and based on merit.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH will continue to work with partner organisations to step up efforts in public education, stigma reduction, prevention, testing, treatment and counselling support.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But beyond this, how each of us as individuals relate to persons with HIV also matters a lot.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Here, I would like to appeal to Singaporeans to stand in support of these affected individuals and our efforts to fight the stigma against persons living with HIV.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The welfare of the affected individuals in this incident would be something of deep concern for us.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We would like to encourage those with concerns to contact us at our hotline at, again, 6325 9220.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: You may also call the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS), TAFEP and Action for AIDS, or approach the healthcare institutions and professionals that have been providing you care and support.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am sorry that these irresponsible actions of one of our officers has resulted in such distress to the affected persons.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ler’s case is now before the Courts and he will be dealt with according to the law.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: He had already spent time behind bars here for his earlier offences, and we will spare no efforts in bringing him to justice again for his latest crime.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As individuals and part of the larger Singaporean community, the best way for us to respond to this incident is with sensitivity, understanding and support for those affected.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If we can say no to discrimination and reduce the stigma surrounding HIV, we can turn the harm and discord which the perpetrators seek to sow into a more inclusive and supportive environment for persons with HIV.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The agency involved will assess the damage, prevent further losses and take precautionary measures to heighten safeguards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government Technology Agency (GovTech) will put other agencies across the Government on alert and also take broader measures, if need be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A Police report will be made if there is suspected foul play or loss of physical equipment, such as laptops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Post-breach, the agency affected will undertake a comprehensive review of the incident to understand what more could be done to prevent such an incident and what could be done better to manage such an incident.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Such a review would include the approach taken to inform affected individuals and the public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: At any of the decision junctures that the Minister had to consider over the last few years regarding this case, did the Ministry ever consult any persons with HIV or HIV advocacy groups for their views on whether disclosure should happen and, if so, what views were expressed by these groups or persons?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Second, in light of the move to destigmatise, the policy decision that HIV should be destigmatised in Singapore, and this should be reflected in employment and in other areas of life, would it be appropriate to review, for example, immigration and employment regulations of foreigners regarding HIV as well, at this juncture?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the consultation with other organisations, as the Member would appreciate, this is a very sensitive area.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We had information about Brochez and Ler, and both were being charged in Court.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We were discussing within the Ministry, with people who had been dealing with persons with HIV.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we were familiar with the concerns about the patients, and it was borne out with the issues that arose as a result of this disclosure.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We were, therefore, quite clear that the pressure, the distress and the anxiety were real.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: With regard to destigmatisation of HIV persons and whether we would review the immigration policies, we do these reviews quite regularly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Every time, we would look at the practice here and around the world and take into account the concerns and interests of Singaporeans and decide on these issues.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have made adjustments along the way, as we have done so over the past few years.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I had explained, HIV remains a very serious infectious disease.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we need to be very cautious in approaching this issue.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Australia and New Zealand also have restrictions on long-term stays for persons with HIV.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first is, for those who have been contacted by Brochez and do not report to MOH, and if there is any leakage of personal information, would the person be liable for prosecution?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That means, if the person is contacted by Brochez, given links online to confidential information online, would the person be liable for prosecution if that person did not report to MOH that correspondence, that contact?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question is: I am assuming that NPHU also kept a list of people living with other infectious diseases like sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) and tuberculosis (TB).

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Were any of these lists also compromised by Ler and Brochez?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: NPHU oversees public health issues which would include infectious diseases, such as Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS), Bird Flu, TB, STDs and HIV.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Unit will handle many of these infectious diseases and that is part of the information and data that officers would be handling.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As to the data that has been exposed, it is limited to the HIV Registry, as I had mentioned.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The other question on whether a person receiving information or a link that is provided by Brochez, whether it is illegal to retain them, I have to consult my colleague.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But my suggestion is, whether it is legal or illegal, please forward it to us or to the Police so that we can follow up to investigate the implications of that.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister Shanmugam, your response on the point of law.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But as the Minister has said, if it is sent to MOH, I do not see AGC taking action in those circumstances.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I have two questions for the Minister for Health.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The first is, we are all aware of the painstaking efforts we have taken over the decades to allow people who have or suspect that they may have HIV to come forward for testing.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: So, given this latest incident, what specific measures is the Ministry taking to make sure that these decades of efforts have not been negated?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The second question is that given the requirement for long-term residency and HIV being an issue, which obviously created that whole fraud on the part of Brochez and Ler, how many cases have we encountered so far where fake blood has been used in order to get access to our long-term residence pass, or in the past, even short-term pass?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But this is, to my memory, the first case that we have seen.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I will check and provide the Member with the information.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We do have anonymous test sites across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we will continue to encourage you to come forward and be tested so that at least you will know your status.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And we also encourage you to seek treatment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When you seek treatment, we will know who you are because we need to provide treatment to the patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will do our utmost to protect the data and the information as much as we can.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Rest assured that we will do what we can to support you.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, the effort is not just the Government's alone.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The society as a whole should come together and show support for these persons living with HIV.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: By showing them support, it will encourage more of them to come forward for testing and, more importantly, for treatment as well.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the constituency I serve, there are persons with HIV.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We work with them, we partner them, they are fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While I recognise that good work has already been done in this area by various organisations, such as Action for AIDS or Catholic AIDS Response Effort, will the Ministry consider formalising and bolstering this process, drawing from good initiatives in other countries?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For example, Living Positive Victoria in Australia has a team of peer navigators who are themselves living with HIV, who work extensively with HIV patients and their families, one-on-one.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, arising from this data leak, will MOH consider a more formalised process of support for those living with HIV and their families?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Indeed, we will learn from other countries, their experiences and share their practices on how to better support persons living with HIV.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We also work with advocacy groups and support groups, as well as non-government organisations and voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs), to see how we can enable them, how we can support them in the work that they do.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I have mentioned, many of these require collaborative efforts, not just from the Government.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some persons with HIV would feel more comfortable talking to people that they know, people they are more familiar with and, therefore, it is not just the Government doing it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We need to work with multiple agencies, whether it is Action for AIDS, SOS or other VWOs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we take the Member's point and will explore other possibilities.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I just wanted to confirm that that is in place right now.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My third and last question is, based on what I heard from the Minister's timeline – and I stand corrected if I misheard this – the Minister mentioned that Brochez was convicted and sentenced to 28 months in jail in March 2017 and he was released in 2018.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I just wanted to check if he did, in fact, serve the full sentence as per conviction or was the sentence reduced in length or was it because he had already served time when the conviction took place?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the last question, I can confirm with my colleagues.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But I would imagine that it is subject to the normal prison terms where you have remission of a certain period and then he was deported thereafter.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They are limited to a handful of people.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Whenever they need the information, they would have to then access because they are all doing contact tracing, doing analysis, so all of them are actually working on the similar type of matters.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, we also have to understand that Ler was the head of the unit.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, in his particular position, he needs to have oversight of all the work that the staff is working on and, therefore, he would have access to all the information in any case.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it probably does not relate to this particular incident.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The audit trail will also allow us, when something does happen, to look back.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have to take a multi-pronged approach to data security.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The first level is to have a system in place to prevent abuse of data – things like encrypted thumb drives.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, those are important to allow us to prevent attempts to abuse the data or illegal access to data.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The second level is for us to detect should something happen and there are some suspicious activities that are going on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are the audit trails which are important, the documentation which is important.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is why they were charged in Court.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Only when we do these three would we be able to have a robust system of protecting our information.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, if Members bear in mind that Ler himself was the head of the unit, the safeguards that you put in place, even if it is effective, he had the right to access.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Even if you have audit trails, most of the things that he did from our audit over the last few years, when we checked what he did, based on our investigation, they were legitimate work that he was doing with MOH.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Whether or not he was careful in protecting the data that he was using is a separate issue.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Many of these may not be able to stop Ler from doing what he did but the deterrence is an important part to make sure that those who want to try have to be mindful of the penalties that could be imposed on them if they were ever caught.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, these three must work hand in hand to ensure we have a robust system of data security – protection, detection and deterrence.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: One is, may I know what is the risk of potential suicide amongst the affected individuals and what MOH may be doing to provide more support to help them tide over this very difficult period?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Second, quite clearly, from the whole sequence of events, these two individuals, Brochez and Ler, lacked conscience.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: They are recalcitrant, spiteful, committed a very despicable act and, as Minister has mentioned also, despite having systems and policies in place, it did not stop Ler from abusing his position and authority.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: It did not stop Brochez, even with the different time milestones after being discovered, from being willful and spiteful.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, I am wondering whether the current penalties are deemed to be deterrent enough and whether there is scope to enhance the penalties further to prevent such individuals from ever committing such crimes ever again?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They have to sense the distress the patients are facing, and they have to make a judgement how much to tell them, whether to stress them further, or to refer them for help.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Often, when they come across a person who has a clear intention to do something drastic, they would refer them to the Institute of Mental Health, for example, who can manage them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Often, they would try to refer them to people whom they are familiar with, people who have been their support group, so that they are able to continue to support them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But these are very delicate issues, and I do not want to go into specific details for various reasons.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the issue of – what is Member's second question?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is something probably for the Ministry of Law to look into.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we will press for whatever is allowable under the law.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But because Ler's case is still being appealed, I would not want to go into the case's specific details.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will wait for the Court and the law to take its process.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have got two clarifications actually for the Ministry of Communications and Information, so I am not sure whether Minister S Iswaran or Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will take them.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first clarification is that, in this recent incident involving NPHU, the organisation concerned is actually within MOH and, therefore, I would like confirmation that it does not come under the auspices of the PDPA.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second clarification is, earlier Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary went through the IM or some policy about how the public sector safeguards personal data and, if I heard him correctly, a lot of responsibility is placed on the department concerned to assess and come up with measures.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My question is, in this recent incident involving the HIV leak, did any department outside MOH assess whether the arrangements that were in existence at the time when the breach occurred, whether the security arrangements were reasonable?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Did anybody outside MOH come to any conclusion or inquire into the matter?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Those are not the same standards that are present today.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The standards have changed, the training of officers has changed, and the deployment and use of technology have changed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And thereafter, he also had remission, as is usual, which accounted for the dates that the Member had in mind.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Just two supplementary questions for the Minister for Health.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am heartened by the additional measures that the Minister has shared, one of which he mentioned was the setting up of the compliance team.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I want to have a sensing of how big this compliance team is.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My second question is, on the one part we talk about deterrent measures.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: On the other part, for positions within the Ministry which we consider as in possession of sensitive information, I wonder whether we could improve – prior to the appointment of people to these positions, whether we could subject them to additional tests on character, things which can allow us to sharpen the process of appointing these people to these positions.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But for these positions, perhaps it is already in existence, but I would request that perhaps these appointments be subjected to more tests prior to confirmation of their appointment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We would need to look at the scope of the work and determine what is the size that we need.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Policies are as good as how much they are practised on the ground.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, it is important for us to make sure that they practise what the policy requires.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we will have to continue to enhance the size of the group.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the recruitment for staff handling sensitive information, we will take a look.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But there is no foolproof system because integrity of the person has to be tested over time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, sometimes you do the best you can in assessing a person's character, but you will never know until you have worked with him over a period of time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We also have to be careful with unnecessary discrimination when you deal with a character assessment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, in recruitment and selecting people, we would need to take quite a holistic approach and make a holistic assessment on the suitability of the person.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I have two questions to ask the Minister.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: It was reported on the MOH website that Ler has been charged under the OSA for failing to take reasonable care of confidential information regarding HIV-positive patients.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, the critical issue here is not really about failing to take reasonable care of the confidential information.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The issue here is why did the MOH system at NPHU allow someone to download the entire database.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The second issue is, I also read from the MOH website that additional safeguards against mishandling of information by authorised staff were only put in place three to four years after MOH was first alerted to an allegation that Ler had misused the HIV Registry.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I also understand earlier from Minister Iswaran that there are regular mandated IT audits done with regard to security of personal data at our public agencies.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we will need to expand the governance division.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On Mr Png Eng Huat's question, even in 2012, there were data security governance policies at that time stipulated by the Government through the IMs and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: NPHU is compliant with the requirements stipulated in the Government's data governance policies.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, even at that time, you were only allowed to download data onto Government-issued computers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, you were not allowed to download data into your own computers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The nature of Ler's job requires him to constantly operate on the database and, therefore, he is allowed to download the registry into his computer.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Unfortunately, he did not protect the data by using an unencrypted thumb drive.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At that time, we did not have the encrypted thumb drive policy, so he used a normal thumb drive and he did not protect the thumb drive.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you are using the thumb drive, you need to transfer files from computer to another Government computer to work on it, you ought to protect the thumb drive.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The policy stipulates that you must ensure that your access to the confidential official information must be with you all the time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: You must ensure that you have possession of the information all the time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But he was believed to have failed to keep the thumb drive with him at all times and, had therefore, contravened the OSA, and that is why he is charged on that basis.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Can I ask the Minister, with PDPA exemption for MOH, what will be the recourse that the victims can seek as a result of this exposure of sensitive information?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: This is to address public trust for better accountability.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we encourage them to talk to us, and we will discuss with them what are the ways to help them and to support them in whichever way we can.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My question relates to what I understand was the blood test that was done at the clinic where Dr Ler was a locum.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Brochez did the blood test at the clinic where Dr Ler was a locum.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister what are the rules preventing doctors from carrying out test for people they know which may put them in a position of compromise or conflict of interest, or question of independence may be raised exactly in the situation like when Brochez went to take a blood test at the clinic where Dr Ler worked?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And just to supplement, to this end, whether or not the Minister thinks that we need to strengthen the governance in this particular area.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I would need to be careful in answering this because the appeal is still in progress, but I can answer, probably, generally.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Generally, doctors have to exercise discretion and they will have to exercise judgement, too.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Under the ethical codes of conduct and guidelines, they will have to assess whether they do have a conflict of interest.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If they feel that they have a conflict, they ought to make it known to the patient and to then step away from whatever procedure or treatment that they may be offering to them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we cannot have a rule to say that you are not allowed to see everybody you know.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Then, you have a problem, because doctors know many people.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, eventually, it is the judgement of the doctor himself to assess whether by treating you, I do have a conflict of interest.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But I must say that, in this particular case, it is not the conflict of interest, it is more than that.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Brochez has been charged for cheating for fraud for specific reasons.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is not just a conflict of interest.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In Brochez's case, and the case is over.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Out of the 2,500 that MOH has contacted, has any of them been contacted and blackmailed?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Was there any demand made on them in the first place?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The Minister mentioned that there were a few of them that were given the link.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: When they were given the link, what was the demand?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Part of this is part of the Police investigation that is ongoing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Maybe I can just say that Brochez is not very consistent in his communication with all the relevant parties.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I probably should not go too much into the mechanism and the process because this is part of the Police investigation work that is ongoing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This is a question about Government disclosure policy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I agree that, in this case, the Government had to make a very difficult decision to balance transparency with the interest of those affected, and I do not want to second-guess that decision.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These issues tend to vary from issue to issue, from case to case.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, it is not that there are no guidelines; it is not a vacuum.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.41 pm until 4.00 pm.
